target.title: fix: Control UI avatar initial breaks on emoji display names
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI rendered a broken/garbled avatar initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half / replacement character) instead of the intended glyph. This PR fixes that by using `Intl.Segmenter` to extract complete grapheme clusters.

## Summary

- **Problem**: Avatar initial used `.slice(0, 1)` (first UTF-16 code unit), breaking on emoji/astral Unicode.
- **Solution**: New `deriveAvatarInitial` helper using `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"`. Falls back to surrogate-pair-aware extraction for browsers without `Intl.Segmenter` (Firefox 114-124).
- **What changed**:
  - `ui/src/lib/avatar.ts` — `deriveAvatarInitial` with feature detection + fallback (no behavior change for ASCII)
  - `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — sidebar chip avatar uses helper
  - `ui/src/components/agent-select.ts` — agent selector fallback uses helper
  - `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-agent-menu.ts` — agent menu row initial uses helper
  - `ui/src/pages/agents/panels-overview.ts` — agents overview identity editor avatar uses helper
  - `ui/src/e2e/avatar-initial-emoji.e2e.test.ts` — dedicated real-Chromium E2E covering all four surfaces
- **All four call sites now share the identical `(deriveAvatarInitial(...) || "?")` empty-input fallback** for consistent behavior.
- **What did NOT change**: ASCII names; other `.slice()` sites (ASCII-only inputs); the plugin monogram in `ui/src/pages/plugins/presentation.ts` (see coordination note).

## Rebased onto current `main`

Rebased onto current `main` (`55a822dc687`). The upstream `app-sidebar.ts` refactor (now extending `AppSidebarMenusElement`, ~688 LOC) moved the chip-avatar fallback; the affected call site still exists and was reapplied at `app-sidebar.ts:615-617`. Import-block conflict from the refactor was resolved manually. The rebased diff against `main` is exactly the 8 files above (+319 / -7).

## The four affected surfaces

A full scan of remaining `.slice(0, 1)` avatar-initial fallback sites found all four **live** surfaces sharing the identical bug:

- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — sidebar chip avatar
- `ui/src/components/agent-select.ts` — agent selector dropdown fallback
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-agent-menu.ts` — agent menu row initial
- `ui/src/pages/agents/panels-overview.ts` — agents overview identity editor avatar

All now route through `deriveAvatarInitial` and are covered by the E2E below.

## Browser Compatibility

- **With `Intl.Segmenter`** (Firefox 125+, Chrome 87+, Safari 14.1+): complete grapheme clusters preserved (emoji, joined emoji, flags, skin-tone).
- **Without `Intl.Segmenter`** (Firefox 114-124): first complete code point extracted (surrogate-pair-aware), no garbled surrogate half.

## Evidence

**Real browser proof** (Playwright real Chromium, mocked Gateway), all four avatar surfaces, captured on the rebased `main`:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_UI_PROOF=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \

✓ renders the emoji grapheme initial in the sidebar chip and agent menu row
✓ renders the emoji grapheme initial in the agent selector dropdown
✓ renders the emoji grapheme initial in the agents overview identity editor
3 passed
```

Each surface's rendered avatar text is asserted `.toBe("🚀")` — the intact grapheme cluster, not a dangling surrogate half — read from the real browser DOM. Full-page screenshots captured locally (NOT committed, per repo visual-proof policy): `.artifacts/control-ui-e2e/avatar-initial-emoji/{01-sidebar-chip-emoji,02-agent-selector-emoji,03-agents-overview-emoji}.png`.

**Unit + component tests**:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts
20 passed
```

Helper unit tests cover both the `Intl.Segmenter` path and the stubbed-`undefined` fallback path (emoji, ZWJ family, flags, skin-tone, ASCII, empty/null/undefined). Typecheck `pnpm tsgo:ui` exit 0; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean on touched files.

target.body:
Fixes #107788

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users asking a question that the agent delegates to a background subagent (`sessions_spawn` + `sessions_yield` with an interim message like "Research started — I'll send the results shortly") would see nothing at all: the yield acknowledgment was never delivered, and the chat stayed silent for minutes until the subagent's announce arrived. The model believes the ack was shown (the tool result echoes it), so it never re-sends it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The yield `message` died in two places: the embedded runner persisted it only as a hidden (`display: false`) context message (`attempt.sessions-yield.ts:persistSessionsYieldContextMessage`), and the Codex app-server wrapper dropped the string entirely (`onYieldDetected` took no argument). Neither harness carried it into the run result, so the reply pipeline's empty-payload exit (`agent-runner.ts`) returned silence.

Following the triage's recommended shape: both harnesses now carry an optional `yieldMessage` as an attempt-result fact next to the existing `yieldDetected`/`meta.yielded` boolean, and the canonical reply pipeline emits it once — only when the turn yielded, is interactive (external-user provenance; subagent runs and heartbeats stay silent), and produced no other user-visible delivery. The reply runner owns the "what to deliver for an empty run" semantic (it already synthesizes the empty-interactive fallback there); this PR adds the yield case beside it and leaves announce semantics, yield context persistence, and fence/admission behavior intact.

One subtlety the delivery guard must get right: `hasVisibleOutboundDeliveryEvidence`/`hasCompletedTerminalDeliveryEvidence` count **accepted session spawns** and cron adds as delivery evidence (replay-safety semantics, not user visibility). A spawn-and-yield turn always has an accepted spawn, so gating the ack on those helpers makes the fix a no-op in exactly the reported scenario — the live-gateway run below demonstrates this. The ack therefore gates only on strictly user-visible evidence (streamed terminal blocks, source replies, visible message-tool sends, approval prompts). This is also the material difference from #108540, whose `hasVisibleDelivery` gate includes `successfulSideEffectDelivery`/`successfulTerminalDelivery` (both spawn-contaminated) and whose regression test mocks the yielded turn without `acceptedSessionSpawns`.

Non-goals: no change to the hidden yield context message, subagent announce delivery, heartbeat semantics, or any config/env surface; the new meta field is additive and consumed per attempt (no registry, no cache).

## User Impact

When an agent spawns background work and yields with a message, that message now reaches the user immediately as a normal reply (chunking/threading/dedupe apply). Spawn-and-yield turns no longer look like delivery failures.

## Evidence

Real behavior — gateway + qa-channel + mock-openai provider driving the exact reported flow (inbound DM → `sessions_spawn` → `sessions_yield` with message → zero assistant payloads), fresh dist build for each run:

target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

This reproduces the linked incident's shape — and its failure mode fired en masse:

14:35:0x  parent spawns 8 investigators (2 batches), yields
14:40–14:53  11 child runs end (incl. parent-driven re-dispatches); EIGHT completion

The retry hardening (second commit) exists because an earlier identical run showed the one-shot wake turn dying to the same provider stall and re-parking the session — the retry + fresh-suffix idempotency design was validated live within the same evening.

**After-fix real-run proof #1 — clean mechanics (2026-07-03, redacted):** same setup, one user message: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. ```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. In this run the parent synthesized correctly on the final announce turn itself; the settle wake then fired at drain exactly as designed — one turn, batch-stable `requester-settle` key covering all three children, full findings attached — and its `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message. That is the designed division of labor: when the parent handles the last announce well (as here), the wake is a silent no-op; when it doesn't (the production incident replied `NO_REPLY`/mis-tracked on the final announce and parked for 5.5 minutes), the wake is the turn that forces the synthesis, carrying everything needed to produce it.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).
- **Trigger seams** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`): fires from `completeCleanupBookkeeping` (the funnel all cleanup-terminal paths share) and from `suspendPendingFinalDelivery`; the suspended-delivery discard sweep passes `skipRequesterSettleWake` so a 24 h-later discard cannot re-wake. Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Transient-failure retry** (second commit): the settle wake is the only event that ever fires after a drain, so a wake turn lost to a provider stall would re-park the requester permanently (observed live — see Evidence). Bounded recovery: up to 3 attempts with 30 s/120 s backoff, each retry under a fresh `:retry-N` idempotency suffix (the gateway dedupe caches terminal run outcomes per key, so re-dispatching the same key would no-op). A legitimately silent wake reply already classifies as delivered and never retries; terminal failures and an abandoned requester stop immediately.
- **Why source, not a prompt/dist mitigation:** parking is *defined by* no turn running, so prompt-assembly mitigations can only decorate turns that occur — they cannot create the wake turn. A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).
- Release note: fixed top-level sessions parking after parallel subagent fan-outs — the requester is now woken to synthesize when its last child settles, including when a child's completion announce gave up.

target.title: feat(claude): add claude-bridge app-server harness extension
target.body:
## Summary

TL;DR:
Inspiration: https://openclaw.ai/blog/openai-models-in-openclaw-done-right; goal: achieve parity for Claude

New feature; issue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93793

OpenClaw currently has no first-class harness for Anthropic models. Anthropic users either fall back to a generic provider client (no native tool execution, no extended-thinking awareness, no per-turn rate-limit surfacing) or run a Claude harness out-of-tree with no contract for OpenClaw's plugin-SDK capabilities and features.

The codex harness already ships in-tree with the same shape we want — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/` is a codex-app-server JSON-RPC client over stdio. We have a working Anthropic-side equivalent built and running in production on the author's setup; opening it for maintainer steer before doing more SDK work on top.

Harness: this PR
JSON-RPC server: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge

**What is the intended outcome?**

- Bundled extension `@openclaw/claude` registers `claude-bridge` as a harness option in the model picker.
- At turn-start, the extension spawns an `openclaw-claude-bridge` subprocess and speaks the codex-shaped JSON-RPC protocol over stdio, directly wrapping the latest claude agent SDK. The server (currently published as `@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge`  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge — fork-preview path; would migrate to `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` if the maintainers republish it) handles Anthropic API I/O, rate-limit surfacing, image-payload sanitization, and plugin-thread-config persistence.
- Bridge-side handles event projection into OpenClaw's notification/accumulator surface, transcript mirroring with idempotency keys, dynamic-tool aggregate output cap, vision-tools de-duplication, and `/claude` slash commands.
- See `extensions/claude/README.md` for the full feature map.

**What is intentionally out of scope?**

- Republishing the server under `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` — needs maintainer decision; the `@zeroaltitude` scope dependency is the current placeholder.
- Migrating to OpenClaw's standard plugin-SDK provider hooks beyond what `extensions/codex/` already uses. The bridge follows codex's pattern verbatim where applicable.
- Anything outside the harness bridge surface.

**What does success look like?** Anthropic users get parity with codex users: native tool dispatch, rate-limit-aware errors, extended-thinking-friendly transcript mirroring, harness-level event projection. No regressions to existing harnesses.

**What should reviewers focus on?**

1. **Scope concern — am I taking too much core?** The branch touches `src/plugins/command-registration.ts`, `src/plugins/current-plugin-metadata-snapshot.ts`, `src/plugins/agent-tool-result-middleware-types.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.ts`, `src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.ts`, and `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`. Each is small and necessary to wire a harness extension, but the contribution guide says "one thing per PR." Happy to split into prep PRs first if maintainers prefer.
2. **External-plugin vs. bundled-extension** — Per CONTRIBUTING.md "most features should be third-party plugins." Open to packaging this entirely as an external plugin instead of `extensions/claude/`, if that is preferred.
3. **Anthropic-API behavior delegated to a separate server repo** — Most of the actual API logic lives in the server (https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw-plugins/tree/main/openclaw-claude/server -- https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge). Reviewers will probably want to inspect that companion repo before approving.
4. **`claude-bridge` harness id naming** — there's no precedent for "<vendor>-bridge" harness names; renamable. (The reason I did this initially was to ensure that I wasn't representing that this work was by anthropic -- matters more on the server naming than the in-openclaw extension tho)

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Anthropic-model agents previously had no in-tree harness; the bridge unlocks native tool runs against Claude through the same JSON-RPC pattern codex uses.
- **Real environment tested:** Author's openclaw gateway running on Linux (WSL2 / Ubuntu), Node 22.x. Author's agents  are configured with `claude-bridge` as their harness and are in daily active use against `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
  2. `openclaw gateway restart --deep`
  3. Send a Slack DM to one of the claude-bridge agents
  4. Agent responds with native Anthropic tools used; transcript file contains the projected events.
  5. `/claude status` in the same thread prints shared-client liveness.
- **Evidence after fix (fresh capture, 2026-05-28):** This gateway runs the claude-bridge harness as the default runtime for all Anthropic models (`agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.id = "claude-bridge"`), so the harness is exercised continuously across multiple agents. Captured live:
  1. **Bridge liveness** — shared-client lifecycle today: `claude-bridge: spawned ×5 / initialized ×5 / process exited ×5` (restarts and re-initializes without manual intervention).
  2. **A turn completing with visible tool/progress output** — one bridge turn dispatching consecutive tools, each completing, with per-tool provenance timing from the observability plugin: `ToolSearch → after_tool_call 1.9ms`, `exec → 1.7ms`, `Write → 1.9ms`, `Agent → 1.9ms`.
  3. **Transcript / result event stream** — the run persists a projected event stream to `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/sessions/<uuid>.jsonl`: parentId-chained `message` events covering the user turn, assistant `tool_use` blocks, and `tool_result` blocks.
  4. **`/claude status`** (live, from a bridge-backed agent):
     ```
     Claude app-server status
     Shared client: running
     Command: openclaw-claude-bridge
     Last stderr: [turn-runner] system event {"subtype":"init"} / {"subtype":"status"} / unhandled SDK event {"type":"rate_limit_event"}
     ```
  *Log-hygiene note:* a few `claude-bridge: runAttempt failed` lines appear in the same logs; they are not bridge defects — one class is a context-overflow on a zero-message scheduled run (auto-compaction correctly skipped), the other is transient model-call failover during an MCP reconnect; both recovered on the next turn. Earlier daily-driver context still applies: Tabitha (claude-bridge) has been in active production use for ~2 weeks.
- **Observed result after fix:** Anthropic turns complete normally; tool calls fire; rate-limit messages are user-actionable; resume across restart works via the `.claude-binding.json` sidecar.
- **What was not tested:**
  - Windows/macOS gateway hosts (only Linux/WSL2 verified).
  - Bun runtime (Node 22 only).
  - Anthropic enterprise/Bedrock/Vertex API surfaces (only public Anthropic API).
  - Concurrent multi-account scenarios beyond 3 agents.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Author runs a single-host gateway. The server is currently published under the author's `@zeroaltitude` npm scope (fork-preview), so reproducing this requires installing the bridge from that scope until maintainers republish.
- **Before evidence:** N/A — no prior in-tree harness for Anthropic to compare against.

## Tests and validation

- Real world use for over a month on a broad diversity of tasks with observed, anecdotal, improvements in coding, token usage and well executed long running tasks
- `pnpm build` ✓ (local)
- `pnpm test extensions/claude` ✓ (local — extension unit tests, including event projector, dynamic-tools middleware port, thread fork policy envelope, transcript mirror dedupe)
- `pnpm test:extensions` not run since last rebase — recommend Testbox/Crabbox run before non-draft review.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit per contributor rule; maintainer to add on land.

## Risk checklist

- **Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes — new `claude-bridge` harness appears in model picker; new `/claude` slash command surface.
- **Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** Yes — new plugin `configSchema` (see `extensions/claude/openclaw.plugin.json`). Existing agent configs unaffected unless they explicitly opt into `claude-bridge` harness. Doctor contract added (`extensions/claude/doctor-contract-api.ts`).
- **Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** Yes (intentional). The bridge spawns a subprocess that holds the Anthropic API key in-memory and makes network calls to Anthropic. Subprocess lifecycle is owned by the harness, not user shell. The plugin SDK enabler changes (e.g. `command-registration.ts`) are additive and follow existing codex-extension precedent.
- **Highest-risk area:** Server-bridge stdio lifecycle and the few SDK enabler edits in `src/plugins/**`. If the SDK changes accidentally relax a guard for non-claude paths, every harness would inherit the change.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The SDK changes are narrowly scoped — each follows a codex-extension-shaped precedent. Happy to factor them into a prep PR if reviewers want to land them separately first.

## Current review state

- **Next action:** Maintainer steer on scope: (a) accept as bundled extension as-is, (b) split SDK enablers into a prep PR first, or (c) request packaging as an external plugin.
- **Still waiting on:** Maintainer decision on the above. CI run on this push.
- **Bot/reviewer comments addressed:** None yet — opening draft.

---

🤖 **AI-assisted disclosure:** Developed with the assistance of Claude Code (anthropic.com/claude-code). All design decisions, production deployment, and real-behavior verification are human-driven; AI assistance was used for implementation across multiple sessions. Session transcripts available on request.

target.title: fix(media-understanding): apply image compression policy to media:// references
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: media:// image references, explicit model calls, and CLI infer image describe all bypassed image compression policy, causing oversized photos to fail with provider dimension limit errors
- Solution: Resolve image compression policy from two sources — configured model metadata (openclaw.json) + bundled static catalog — and apply it via optimizeImageBufferForWebMedia before provider execution. Covers all three entry points: channel-triggered media:// references, runtime API describeImageFileWithModel, and CLI infer image describe --model.
- What changed: 6 files (+110/-100 relative to original PR head, +126/-14 net vs main at time of original PR)
  - runner.entries.ts: resolveImageCompressionPolicyFromConfig now merges configured model limits (cfg.models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.image) with bundled static catalog limits. Configured takes priority; catalog fills gaps.
  - runtime.ts: imports the shared helper from runner.entries; passes provider/model through prepareImageDescriptionInput to resolve model-aware policy
  - capability-cli.ts: passes activeModel.provider/model into prepareImageDescriptionInput so catalog/config limits are resolved for CLI image describe
  - runner.test-mocks.ts: add applySecretRefHeaderSentinels to model-auth mock (upstream compat)
  - runner.vision-skip.test.ts: add media-services.js + provider-secret-egress mocks (upstream compat)
  - apply.test.ts: add createImageProcessor/readImageProbe mocks and adapt HEIC test expectations (upstream compat)
- What did NOT change: image tool (resolveCompressionModelPolicy unchanged), HEIC normalization boundary, web-media helpers, config surface

Fixes #101923

## Root Cause

- resolveImageCompressionPolicyFromConfig only read agents.defaults (preferredSidePx), producing a policy without hard maxSidePx/maxPixels. optimizeImageBufferForWebMedia preserves originals when no hard constraints exist, so provider-specific dimension caps (e.g. Anthropic 2576px maxSidePx) were bypassed.
- The CLI --model path also called preparation before provider/model were known, so the model-catalog lookup could not resolve.
- Missing detection: no test verifying media-understanding applies the same model-aware policy as the image tool.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Oversized images reaching media-understanding providers without compression, bypassing provider dimension caps
- **Real environment tested:** Linux Node 22, pnpm install + pnpm build, worktree isolation
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```bash
# Generate oversized test image
convert -size 4096x4096 xc:red /tmp/test-oversized-4096.png
# Run integrated pipeline with model-aware policy
```
- **Evidence after fix:**
```
BEFORE: /tmp/test-oversized-4096.png PNG 4096x4096
POLICY: {"quality":"balanced","models":[{"preferredSidePx":2048},{"maxSidePx":2576,"preferredSidePx":2576}]}
AFTER: /tmp/test-optimized.png JPEG 2048x2048
VERDICT: 4096x4096 → 2048x2048 ✅
```
- **Observed result after fix:** 4096x4096 PNG compressed to 2048x2048 JPEG. Policy merges agents.defaults (preferredSidePx:2048) with bundled static catalog mediaInput.image (maxSidePx:2576 from anthropic/claude-sonnet-5) and configured model metadata when present. All three code paths now pass provider/model into compression resolution.
- **What was not tested:** Live provider execution (no API keys). Image processing pipeline and policy resolution validated through unit tests; the compression path reuses the same web-media helpers and catalog lookup the image tool already exercises in live calls.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit tests across media-understanding test files
- Test files and pass counts:
  - runtime.test.ts: 21/21 — image normalization, HEIC bypass, remote references
  - runner.vision-skip.test.ts: 18/18 — provider routing, native vision skip, MiniMax VLM fallback
  - runner.entries.guards.test.ts: 12/12 — entry guard invariants
  - apply.test.ts: 54/54 — attachment transcription, local binary probing, HEIC images
  - image-tool.test.ts: 94/94 — sibling image-tool compression policy contract
  - **Total: 199/199 passing**
- Upstream compat fixes: pre-existing test failures from upstream secret-sentinel changes (RastermillError in vision-skip/apply tests due to missing media-services mocks) are also resolved.

## Risk checklist

- **Backward compatibility:** ✅ optional opts added; callers without provider/model get config-only behavior
- **Config contract:** ✅ reads existing agents.defaults + cfg.models.providers (no new config surface)
- **Provider contracts:** ✅ respects catalog mediaInput.image limits; configured limits take priority
- **HEIC conversion:** ✅ preserved (optimization runs before HEIC normalization)
- **Performance:** ✅ process-stable catalog lookup + config property reads; no async I/O added
- **Side effects:** ✅ only media-understanding image paths
- **Image tool unaffected:** ✅ resolveCompressionModelPolicy unchanged

target.title: fix(browser): keep CDP cursor text previews UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`findCursorInteractiveElements` truncates DOM text inside a **browser** `Runtime.evaluate` page expression with `.slice(0, 101)`. At an emoji/surrogate boundary that cut can leave a **lone high surrogate** on the CDP `returnByValue` wire. Node `truncateUtf16Safe(..., 100)` is a **no-op** when the string is already `length === 100`, so the malformed unit survives. Approaches that *call* Node/SDK `truncateUtf16Safe` **inside** the page expression throw `ReferenceError` and fail closed to an empty cursor map.

## Why This Change Was Made

Own the cut in a **page-local**, dependency-free helper injected via `Function#toString`, with a unified page/Node preview budget of **100**.

**Stronger than [#108316](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/108316):** that helper only rewinds when the cut splits a live surrogate pair (`end < length` and next is low). This tip also **scrubs a trailing high surrogate when `length === max` already holds a lone unit** (the exact residue unsafe `.slice` leaves and Node cannot repair). Helper lives in `cdp-page-text-preview.ts` imported by `cdp.ts` so Knip/`deadcode:exports` sees a production consumer (fixes the unused-export CI failure from exporting off `cdp.ts`).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal container sends could apply the wrong styled span when `text-style` start/length tokens used JavaScript-only forms such as `0x10` or `1e1`. Those tokens were coerced with `Number(...)` into different offsets, so bold/italic markers could land on the wrong characters or invent spans that the caller never intended.

## Why This Change Was Made

target.title: fix(secrets): inactive web refs no longer block agent turns
target.body:
Related: #105536

## Summary

Accept locally classified inactive SecretRefs as terminal when a successful Gateway `secrets.resolve` response contains only a partial command snapshot.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ordinary agent turns could fail before model execution when a disabled or non-selected web provider retained a SecretRef and the active Gateway returned a valid but incomplete secrets snapshot.

## Root Cause

PR #105160 changed the Gateway command resolver to preserve authoritative assignments from partial runtime snapshots. That made the caller's targeted local-fallback merge reachable for paths omitted by a successful Gateway response.

Before this change, that merge accepted only `resolved_local`. The existing local resolver correctly classified omitted disabled-provider paths as `inactive_surface`, but the merge ignored that terminal state and relabeled the path unresolved. In strict agent preparation, it then threw `is unresolved in the active runtime snapshot` before the agent run began.

The related #105536 addresses how new runtime snapshots collect inactive web-provider credentials. This change is complementary: it repairs the established partial-result fallback contract even when a Gateway snapshot omits an inactive path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The partial-result merge now handles both locally materialized values and locally proven inactive paths. Genuine unresolved paths keep the existing strict failure behavior, and the local-resolution summary still counts only paths that materialized a value.

## User Impact

Agent turns no longer fail merely because an inactive web provider credential is absent from an otherwise valid partial Gateway snapshot. Missing credentials on active surfaces still fail as before.

## Evidence

On current `main`, the added regression failed with 1 failed / 35 passed and `agent: plugins.entries.google.config.webSearch.apiKey is unresolved in the active runtime snapshot`. With this patch, the focused CLI and runtime-secret command passes both Vitest shards with 40 tests passed; strict preparation records the omitted path as `inactive_surface` with no unresolved targets.

## Real behavior proof

- **Before behavior:** the added focused regression failed on current `main` with 1 failed / 35 passed and `agent: plugins.entries.google.config.webSearch.apiKey is unresolved in the active runtime snapshot`.
- **Exact after-patch command:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/command-secret-gateway.test.ts src/secrets/runtime-command-secrets.test.ts`
- **Copied after result:** 2 Vitest shards passed; 40 tests passed.
- **Observed after behavior:** strict agent preparation returns `hadUnresolvedTargets: false`, preserves the configured SecretRef, records `inactive_surface`, and retains the existing inactive-surface diagnostic.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/command-secret-gateway.test.ts src/secrets/runtime-command-secrets.test.ts` — 40 tests passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/cli/command-secret-gateway.ts src/cli/command-secret-gateway.test.ts` — passed.

A live Telegram turn against a restarted patched Gateway was not run because that would mutate the operator's live service. ## What Problem This Solves

Dedicated Slack **read** WebClients (`createSlackWebClient` / lookup) had no default Axios request timeout (except lookup’s existing 30s). Slow/hung Slack GETs could block indefinitely.

Bolt’s shared `App.client` must **not** inherit that deadline: mutations (reactions, chat.*, streaming) can be committed by Slack before the HTTP response returns; timing out then enables false failures and retries.

## Why This Change Was Made

- lookup → same `SLACK_READ_TIMEOUT_MS`
- write / upload `timeout: 0` unchanged

target.title: fix: queued voice replies are lost when the delivery queue retries them
target.body:
Closes #108501

**Prompt request:** Keep a queued voice reply deliverable after the producer's temporary media is cleaned up and the producer dies, without widening what a send is allowed to read.

**Proof target:** A fresh process recovers byte-identical audio for a queued voice reply whose original temp no longer exists, while immediate sends stay copy-free and live-only media is never persisted.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with automatic TTS would silently lose voice replies whenever the outbound delivery queue retried them.

Automatic TTS synthesizes into a temporary file owned by the producing process, and the raw path of that file is stored in the durable delivery queue. The file is removed when the producer exits, and unconditionally five minutes after synthesis. The queue's own retry budget is roughly 22.5 minutes, so the cleanup lands inside it: later retries read a path that no longer exists. Recovery also commonly runs in a different process than the one that enqueued the entry, and that process never had the temp at all.

The message was already accepted into the write-ahead queue, so the system had effectively promised to deliver it. Instead the reply is dropped. The resulting `Local media file not found` is not classified as a permanent error, so the entry consumes all five retries before being dead-lettered, and the text of the reply is lost along with the audio.

## Why This Change Was Made

The queue now owns the media it promises to replay. Before a deliverable row is published, each authorized local source is read through the same media access the live send already uses and copied into a queue-owned artifact directory; only the queue payload is rewritten to point at that copy. The live send keeps the original path and stays copy-free, so immediate delivery is unchanged.

Staging resolves the media read capability exactly as the live send resolves it, so it can neither reject media the send would deliver nor read more than the send may; both paths now share one resolver instead of keeping separate argument lists.

Ownership is proven by process identity rather than by a marker file, a lease table, or a clock. Artifacts are grouped per producing process generation (`<pid>-<processStartTime>-<nonce>`), and a generation is reclaimed only when its owner is provably gone. A live owner, an owner whose identity cannot be verified, and a recycled PID whose start time no longer matches are each handled without deleting media that a pending row still needs. Wall-clock age is never an ownership signal, so a gateway that has been idle for a long time keeps its own undelivered media.

Ordering is durable-state-first: the row transition commits before any artifact is unlinked, so a crash in between leaves a reclaimable orphan rather than a row whose media is gone. The retain set is re-read after each death proof, because a short-lived producer can commit a row and exit while a sweep is already running; this is sufficient rather than merely narrower, since a process only ever stages into its own generation.

Scope is deliberately narrow: no database schema change, no new status value, no new configuration surface, no public SDK export, and no lease or owner table. Cross-platform owner identity reuses the existing readers — `getFileLockProcessStartTime` on POSIX and `readWindowsProcessStartTimeSync` on Windows — behind one helper, replacing a pairing that `gateway-lock.ts` had previously kept private.

Sensitive media is treated as live-only throughout: it reaches neither the artifact directory nor the row, so a `required` send fails closed before dispatch and a `best_effort` send degrades to live-only rather than persisting a row it cannot replay.

## User Impact

Voice replies that are deferred or retried now actually arrive. Previously they were dropped silently, together with their accompanying text, after burning the full retry budget.

There is one deliberate trade-off. When a local media source cannot be staged — unreadable, unauthorized, or oversized — a `best_effort` send now creates no durable row and is delivered live-only, and a `required` send fails closed before any platform dispatch. Previously both persisted a row referencing the raw source path. That row was never actually replayable: recovery resolves media through the same loader and access policy as the live send, so a source the queue cannot read is one the retry cannot read either, and the old behavior spent all five retries before dead-lettering while also losing the text. The cost is that a transient filesystem error on an otherwise-good file now drops write-ahead protection for that one send. That is preferable to persisting a raw producer-owned path as a fallback, which is exactly the unreplayable row this change exists to eliminate.

## Evidence

Verified on `2026.7.2`, Node 24.15.0, Linux.

**Observable before/after.** Real OpenRouter Kokoro TTS produced a voice payload; the durable row was committed; the producer then parked with a live event loop so OpenClaw's real 5-minute temp cleanup could fire, and was killed with `SIGKILL` (not a clean exit, which would run cleanup hooks a real crash never runs). A genuinely fresh process then replayed the entry through the production Telegram reconnect drain (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/delivery-queue-runtime` → `drainPendingDeliveries`, with no injected delivery implementation, so the runtime lazy-loads the real internal deliver).

Both sides ran the same harness against the same source bytes, with OpenClaw's real 5-minute cleanup observed firing at ~300.2 s in each:

| | before (clean `main`) | after (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| producer temp after cleanup | deleted | deleted |
| producer death | `SIGKILL` | `SIGKILL` |
| fresh-process drain | fails: `file not found \| not-found` | reaches the adapter's `sendVoice` |
| queue-owned copy | none | byte-identical to the source (SHA-256 match) |

Before the change the entry cannot even reach the transport, because resolving the media fails first. After it, the recovered bytes match the original by SHA-256 and size, and the entry reaches the real adapter's outbound request. An earlier run of the same after-fix sequence with a live OpenRouter Kokoro synthesis produced the same result on real provider audio.

**Tests.** The changed-surface suites pass. One case places its media in an agent workspace that is reachable only through the agent-scoped capability — root expansion is disabled and the state directory sits outside the media roots, so nothing else can admit it. That case fails if staging reverts to the raw media access, if the shared resolver is bypassed, or if the agent identity is dropped from it. Also included is a real child-process crash integration test that commits the row, `SIGKILL`s the producer, and proves a fresh process retains the artifact its pending row needs, reads identical bytes after the producer's source is deleted, and drops the artifact once the row is acked.

The safety-critical assertions are mutation-tested: inverting generation ownership, forcing PID-reuse to look alive, removing the atomic rename, removing partial-stage cleanup, disabling the sensitive-media gate, and snapshotting the GC retain set each fail the suite.

**Static gates.** `tsgo` (core and tests), oxlint, oxfmt, `pnpm build` (0 ineffective dynamic imports), 0 import cycles, the database-first legacy-store guard, and the plugin SDK surface check all pass.

**Scope.** 23 files, +1508/-53; production +551/-51, tests +957/-2. One topic: queued outbound media ownership.

**Limitations.**

- Reclamation runs only when ownership is proven dead. A generation is reclaimed when its owner is provably gone or when a live PID's start time no longer matches; a live owner and an owner whose identity cannot be verified are both retained. Retention is therefore conservative by design, and this change does not make on-disk spool storage strictly bounded. An unverifiable owner keeps its generation until ownership can be proven, which is most likely on platforms where process start time depends on external tooling. This is a deliberate bias: retaining an artifact costs disk, while reclaiming one that a pending row still needs costs the user's message. A size quota is intentionally not part of this change, since fail-closed admission would introduce a separate path that drops durability.
- Reclamation runs from gateway maintenance, which matches the lifecycle of the queue it serves: every drain and recovery caller is gateway-hosted, so without a gateway a pending row is never replayed either and its media is still required rather than reclaimable.
- End-to-end user receipt of the recovered voice is not claimed here. The proof stops at the real adapter's outbound request boundary.

target.title: fix(daemon): prove Windows schtasks launch without foreground listener [AI]
target.body:
## Summary

- **Behavior addressed:** Windows Scheduled Task install / start / restart paths previously skipped the fallback launch whenever any process was already bound to the configured gateway port — even when that process was unrelated to OpenClaw (e.g. `wslrelay.exe`, `docker-proxy.exe`, a developer's local app). The fallback port-ownership check was unverified.
- **Why this matters now:** Operators running OpenClaw on Windows hosts that also have WSL relay services or other TCP servers on the same port (commonly 18789) saw the daemon silently skip the scheduled-task fallback and never start the gateway, leading to a stuck "scheduled task installed but not running" state.
- **Intended outcome:** The fallback path captures a baseline of pre-existing listeners on the port before spawning, then filters those baseline PIDs out of the post-spawn listener detection, so the daemon only treats a listener as "OpenClaw-owned" if it was not present in the baseline AND its argv matches the installed gateway command.
- **Out of scope:** No changes to the scheduled task install / uninstall logic, the fallback spawn command itself, or the gateway server's port-binding behavior.

## Linked context

Closes #91144

## Real behavior proof

target.title: fix(daemon): gateway fails to launch on Windows when the profile path contains CJK characters
target.body:
Closes #107416

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Windows users whose profile path contains CJK characters (e.g. `C:\Users\苗振`) can install OpenClaw but the gateway never starts: the first run fails with a "The system cannot find the file specified" / "找不到 …\gateway.vbs" popup and the Scheduled Task never launches the gateway. Reported against v2026.7.1 on Windows 11 with a Chinese-locale profile path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The daemon writes the generated launchers (`gateway.cmd`, the hidden `gateway.vbs` introduced by #95480, and the Startup-folder fallback entry) as UTF-8 without BOM, but neither Windows script host reads that encoding: `wscript.exe` parses `.vbs` only as ANSI or UTF-16 LE with BOM, and `cmd.exe` parses `.cmd` in the console (OEM) code page. CJK path bytes inside the launchers garble and the launch chain breaks at the first hop.

This PR adds `src/daemon/launcher-encoding.ts` — a per-format encoder plus a BOM-sniffing decoder — used at the three launcher write sites and the `readScheduledTaskCommand` parse site in `src/daemon/schtasks.ts`:

- `.vbs` → always UTF-16 LE with BOM, the one wscript encoding that is correct on every locale.
- `.cmd` → ASCII content stays byte-identical UTF-8 (zero change for non-CJK installs). Non-ASCII content is encoded with the system ANSI code page, but only on locales where ANSI == OEM (936/932/949/950/874/GB18030 — the locales where a code-page fix is well-defined). windows-125x locales keep UTF-8: their console OEM page (437/850/852/866…) differs from ANSI and has no WHATWG decoder, so ANSI bytes would just be a different flavor of wrong there. Encoded output is round-trip-verified with the same decoder the read path uses; unmappable characters fail the install with a clear error instead of writing a silently broken launcher.
- Read-back BOM-sniffs UTF-16, then tries strict UTF-8 first (covers ASCII and all pre-fix installs with no code page probe on the frequent poll path), then falls back to the ANSI code page — so repair/update parses legacy files fine and rewrites the state-dir launchers in the new encodings.

**Design notes:**

- **Why not UTF-16 for `.cmd`:** `cmd.exe` cannot parse UTF-16 batch files (NUL bytes break the parser).
- **Why iconv-lite:** encoding to GBK/Big5/… is required and `TextDecoder` only decodes. `iconv-lite@0.7.2` is already in the dependency tree (`express` → `body-parser`/`raw-body`), so promoting it to a root dependency resolves to the already-locked version and adds no new packages — the `npm-shrinkwrap.json` delta is one line. If a no-new-root-dependency route is preferred, the alternative is keeping `.cmd` UTF-8 and prepending `@chcp 65001>nul`; that mutates the console code page for child processes and relies on cmd's re-read behavior, but I am happy to switch if maintainers prefer it.
- **Code page detection** reuses the existing cached `resolveWindowsSystemEncoding()` in `src/infra/windows-encoding.ts` (now exported); no new detection code.
- **Known sibling surface (explicit follow-up, not in this PR):** `src/infra/windows-task-restart.ts` writes its temp restart `.cmd` as UTF-8 with the same class of embedded paths, so the update-time restart path on CJK hosts needs the same treatment. Kept out to hold this PR to one concern; I can file the follow-up issue once this lands.

## User Impact

Windows users with CJK (or Thai) characters anywhere in their profile/state path can now install and start the gateway, and gateway repair/update migrates existing broken installs by rewriting the state-dir launchers. Users with pure-ASCII paths get byte-identical launcher files — no change at all.

## Evidence

- New unit coverage `src/daemon/launcher-encoding.test.ts` (12 tests: UTF-16 BOM output incl. a CJK path, ASCII byte-identity under a pinned code page, GBK round-trip, windows-125x gate, unrepresentable-character failure, legacy-UTF-8 and raw-GBK decode).
- Migration coverage in `schtasks.test.ts`: `readScheduledTaskCommand` parses both a legacy UTF-8 CJK script and a GBK-encoded script.
- Install-path coverage in `schtasks.install.test.ts`: the hidden `.vbs` launcher for a CJK profile path starts with `FF FE` and utf16le-decodes to the exact `Run """…""", 0, False` line; an unrepresentable env value fails the install with no launcher file written.
- Focused runs on Windows (Node 24.18, pnpm 11.2.2): launcher-encoding 12/12, schtasks + schtasks.install 48/48, schtasks.startup-fallback + service-env + windows-encoding 137/137; `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files; `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:test:src` clean; `deps:shrinkwrap:root:check` reports current. (`schtasks.stop.test.ts` shows 4 failures on this host that reproduce identically on unmodified `main` — pre-existing and unrelated.)
- Real-machine smoke test on Chinese Windows 10 (ACP=OEMCP=936, the reporter's locale family): a `gateway.vbs`/`gateway.cmd` pair written under `%TEMP%\苗振\` with the new encoder launches via `cscript gateway.vbs` and the payload creates `proof.txt`; the same pair written the old way (plain UTF-8) fails with `gateway-old.vbs(1, 1) (null): The system cannot find the file specified.` — the exact reported symptom — and no proof file appears.

OpenClaw has no structured observability for AI safety-relevant runtime events. When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Telegram TTS final-mode text-before-voice churn on both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths, plus tagged mode partial preview leaking raw `[[tts:text]]` directives, plus media block suppression during captioned final TTS.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout at commit `05b4483a8f`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Live Telegram bot (`@thomas_fu_bot`) with Microsoft TTS (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`), `messages.tts.mode: "final"`.

- **Failing proof before fix (live Telegram)**:

  ![Before fix — separate text message + voice message (churn)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-before-fix.png)

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built and installed from current head: `npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz`
  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait, and it is attributed **per captioned voice payload** rather than by aggregate dispatcher counters:

- Each captioned final (and its synthesized-voice sibling) is tagged with a unique capture token stored in the payload metadata, which survives the dispatcher's internal re-normalization.
- Before enqueue, a per-payload cancelled hook and a per-payload delivery-failed hook are registered, both keyed to that capture token. The delivery-failed hook (`appendReplyDispatcherBeforeDeliverFailed`) is a core-internal observer symmetric to the existing per-payload cancelled hook — it is not part of the plugin-facing dispatcher surface.
- A post-settlement task registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` (the same seam the transcript mirror uses) runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path. It re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final **if and only if this specific captioned voice's own send was cancelled or failed** — never based on the aggregate final-outcome delta.

This matters because a single reply can enqueue multiple finals (a captioned voice plus sibling reasoning/commentary/status finals). The previous aggregate-count comparison mis-attributed a sibling final's failure or cancellation to the captioned voice, re-sending text the voice note had already delivered as its caption — reintroducing the exact churn this PR removes. Per-payload attribution fixes that: recovery follows the captioned voice's own outcome, mirroring the per-send attribution the ACP path already uses. A mixed-outcome regression asserts that a captioned voice which succeeds while a sibling final fails does **not** re-send the caption text. This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

### Cancelled final delivery (not just failed)

A `beforeDeliver` / `reply_payload_sending` hook returning `null` **cancels** a send after `enqueue()` has already reported acceptance. That outcome is tracked as *cancelled*, not *failed* (`getCancelledCounts()` vs `getFailedCounts()` on the dispatcher). The ACP direct-visible-text settlement previously folded only failed counts into its undelivered accounting, so a cancelled captioned voice final left `finalMediaDelivered` set and skipped the deferred text fallback — silently dropping the reply text (the block text was already suppressed for the captioned path).

The settlement now folds cancelled block/final counts alongside failed counts (`settleDirectVisibleText` in `dispatch-acp-delivery.ts`, via a new `readDispatcherCancelledCounts` reader mirroring the failed reader). A cancelled captioned voice final therefore clears `finalMediaDelivered` and the deferred text fallback delivers the accumulated text. The non-ACP path now applies the same per-payload cancelled/failed attribution described above (a cancelled captioned voice recovers its text; a sibling's cancellation does not). A regression test drives an asynchronously cancelled captioned voice on Telegram and asserts the plain-text fallback fires.

Closes #83511

Fixes #108367
Fixes #108473

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users enabling the `cron` tool would get a hard `400` from llama.cpp-backed providers (for example Ornith 1.0) on every agent message. Providers that convert tool JSON Schema to GBNF reject unanchored `pattern` values with `Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'`, so the gateway never reaches model inference.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron schemas advertised a nonblank regex as unanchored `\S`. This change switches those strings to the fully anchored house form `^\S(?:.*\S)?$` already used by worker identifier schemas, and closes the related `^session:.+` pattern with a terminal `$`. Whitespace-only declaration keys and display names still fail validation; normal nonblank values still pass.

## User Impact

Users can keep the `cron` tool enabled with llama.cpp / Ornith-style providers without the gateway failing schema conversion before any reply. Existing cron behavior on providers that already accepted the old patterns is unchanged for normal inputs.

target.title: fix(telegram): keep tool rows visible under progress preambles
target.body:
Related: #106026

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users with `streaming.mode: progress` and verbose output off would see only the model's preamble in the ephemeral progress draft while tools were running. The rolling tool rows were masked until the draft collapsed and the permanent final reply arrived.

The first bad commit is `8d465d71b5f72450a1c71b21f6af6e7e99293759` (#106026). It made a model preamble the status headline, but Telegram's status-headline renderer discarded the accumulated line metadata. The shared compositor also deduplicated only on the unchanged headline text, so later tool rows stopped producing draft updates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram now opts into line-aware updates while a preamble is active and renders bounded structured work rows beneath that headline. Reasoning and commentary remain buffered behind the headline, the configured `maxLines` limit still owns the rolling window, and Discord/Mattermost retain their existing behavior because the new compositor capability is opt-in.

Both Telegram HTML previews and rich-message previews use the same filtered work-row set.

## User Impact

A progress-mode Telegram turn now keeps one ephemeral draft showing the preamble plus the newest configured tool rows (for example, the latest 8 of 10 calls). The existing lifecycle is unchanged: the progress window collapses and the permanent final reply is delivered normally.

## Evidence

- Real pre-fix observation: on OpenClaw 2026.7.2, the Telegram client showed a preamble-only ephemeral draft for the reported turn. The corresponding raw Codex rollout contained the commentary preamble followed by all visible tool-start events, proving the events reached OpenClaw but were masked at draft composition/rendering.
- First-bad source proof: #106026 introduced both the status-headline-only Telegram branch and the text-only compositor dedupe. Its parent had no model-preamble headline path.
- Codex contract proof at upstream Codex `87b808bb57`: `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/event_mapping.rs` maps command starts to `item/started`, while `protocol/v2/item.rs` represents them as `CommandExecution`; OpenClaw's Codex projector normalizes those into `stream: "tool"` start/result events. This confirms the producer contract was intact.
- Added a full callback-chain regression: 10 Codex-style tool starts flow through `createAgentRunEventHandler`, the real buffered reply dispatcher, and Telegram progress rendering with verbose off. It asserts the preamble plus only rows 3-10, permanent final delivery, and a 10-tool collapse summary.
- Added shared compositor coverage for successive line changes under an unchanged preamble.
- Updated both preamble orderings: preamble before tools and preamble after a tool start.

target.title: fix(gateway): scope accumulatedText preservation to media-only replace events
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multimodal agent users on the OpenResponses gateway would see their assistant reply silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emitted a media-only SSE replace event (`replace: true`, `text: ""`) during streaming.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old guard `typeof text === "string"` treated empty string as valid content, unconditionally resetting `accumulatedText` on any `replace: true` event. The fix scopes accumulated-text preservation to media-bearing replacement events by checking for non-empty `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl` — the same media-content signal used by the existing SSE coalesce path (`server-chat.ts:1101`). Non-media empty-text replacement continues to clear the buffer per existing behavior.

## User Impact

Users of multimodal agents (image+text input) on the OpenResponses gateway no longer see their assistant replies silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emits a media-only replace event during streaming.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested**: Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22.22.3 (SQLite 3.51.3), branch `fix/bug-001-accumulatedText-empty-replace`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts
  ```

- **Evidence after fix**:

  ```
  Test Files  3 passed (3)
       Tests  105 passed (105)
  ```

- **Shared code alignment.** The agent runtime producer (`agent-runner-execution.ts:2604`) already guards `replace: true` with a truthy `snapshotText` check. The runtime path at `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.ts:1450` produces the exact `{ text: "", mediaUrls: [...] }` + `replace: true` event shape that this fix targets.

- **What was not tested**: Non-streaming paths (not affected — `accumulatedText` is streaming-only). Real multimodal provider E2E flow (the event shape is produced by the agent runtime, not the provider directly; the mock test exercises the exact runtime event sequence).

### Integrated behavior proof (before vs after)

The fix was verified by temporarily reverting the guard condition and re-running the same test suite:

**Before (old guard — bug):**
```
 FAIL  |gateway-methods| OpenResponses HTTP API (e2e) > preserves accumulated text on media-only replace:true with empty text
AssertionError: expected 'No response from OpenClaw.' to be 'Hello world'

Expected: "Hello world"
Received: "No response from OpenClaw."
```

3 tests failed across 3 gateway shards — all returning `"No response from OpenClaw."` instead of the expected `"Hello world"`.

**After (PR guard — fixed):**
```
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  105 passed (105)
```

All 105 tests pass, including all 3 regression tests for the media-bearing replace path.

### Runtime SSE event trace (with fix applied)

The actual SSE event processing log, captured from the real `handleOpenResponsesHttpRequest` handler during test execution:

```
[e2e-proof] REPLACE text="" hasMediaContent=true  mediaUrls=["https://example.com/image.jpg"] → PRESERVE buffer ("Hello world")
[e2e-proof] FINALIZE phase=end accumulatedText="Hello world"        finalText="Hello world"

[e2e-proof] REPLACE text="" hasMediaContent=false mediaUrls=[]      → CLEAR buffer (was "Hello world")
[e2e-proof] FINALIZE phase=end accumulatedText=""                   finalText="No response from OpenClaw."

[e2e-proof] REPLACE text="" hasMediaContent=false mediaUrl=""       → CLEAR buffer (was "Hello world")
[e2e-proof] FINALIZE phase=end accumulatedText=""                   finalText="No response from OpenClaw."
```

The trace confirms three distinct behaviors:
1. Empty text **with** valid `mediaUrls` → accumulated text **preserved**
2. Empty text with empty `mediaUrls: []` → buffer **cleared** (unchanged behavior)
3. Empty text with empty `mediaUrl: ""` → buffer **cleared** (unchanged behavior)

### Guard condition summary

```
Event shape                                | main (bug)      | PR (fixed)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Empty text + valid mediaUrls             | REPLACE (bug!)  | PRESERVE ✓
Empty text + mediaUrls:[]                | REPLACE         | REPLACE ✓
Empty text + mediaUrl:''                 | REPLACE         | REPLACE ✓
Non-empty text (normal replacement)      | REPLACE         | REPLACE ✓
```

The agent runtime producer code proves that `{ text: "", replace: true, mediaUrls: [...] }` is always a media-only addition, never an intentional text deletion.

### Regression test plan

3 regression tests cover the behavioral surface:
1. Valid `mediaUrls` → text preserved
2. Empty `mediaUrls: []` → text cleared (existing behavior)
3. Empty `mediaUrl: ""` → text cleared (existing behavior)

All 35 gateway tests pass with zero regression.

## Summary

Replaces blocking synchronous filesystem/Keychain I/O with async equivalents in auth/credential paths. Sync `execSync` calls for macOS Keychain access blocked the Node.js event loop for 4+ seconds, causing WebSocket timeouts, infinite pending states, and duplicate message sends under concurrent agent starts.

## Linked context

Closes #78805

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Gateway event loop blocking during credential reads
- Real environment tested: macOS with Claude Code and Codex CLI credentials in Keychain
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```
vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts \
    src/agents/cli-credentials.test.ts \
    src/agents/cli-auth-epoch.test.ts \
    src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.test.ts

vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts \
    src/gateway/resolve-configured-secret-input-string.test.ts
```
- Evidence after fix: 4 test files, 61 tests passed (vitest 4.1.8)
- Observed result after fix: All async credential paths return results without blocking the event loop
- What was not tested: Live Codex Keychain access on real macOS device (unit tests mock exec)
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: Keychain access requires macOS; mocked in CI

## Tests and validation

- Commands: `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-core.config.ts` and `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts`
- Regression coverage: Existing credential reader tests plus new async variant tests
- Before: `execSync("security find-generic-password")` blocked event loop for 4+ seconds
- After: `execAsync` returns immediately without blocking

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? No
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? Yes — credential reads now async
- What is the highest-risk area? Keychain access timeout and error handling
- How is that risk mitigated? Same timeout values, same error paths, just promisified

## Current review state

- Next action: @clawsweeper re-review
- Waiting on: ClawSweeper proof evaluation

Native hook descriptors were not regenerated when the relay was unavailable during gateway restart, causing hooks to silently fail until manual intervention. Falls through to normal OpenClaw policy evaluation instead of hard-blocking when the relay is unavailable.

    src/cli/native-hook-relay-cli.test.ts
```
- Evidence after fix: 1 test file, 20 tests passed (vitest 4.1.8)
- Observed result after fix: Relay unavailability triggers fallthrough to policy evaluation instead of hard-block
- What was not tested: Live relay restart cycle on real Codex harness
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: Relay lifecycle testing requires live Codex; unit tests cover the code path

## Tests and validation

- Commands: `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts`
- Regression coverage: approval-bridge.test.ts covers both error and fallthrough paths
- Before: Relay unavailable at restart → native hook descriptors not regenerated → hooks silently fail
- After: Relay becomes available → descriptors regenerated → hooks work without manual intervention

## Risk checklist

- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? Yes — fallthrough changes approval path
- What is the highest-risk area? Security boundary: falling through to policy evaluation instead of hard-blocking
- How is that risk mitigated? The before_tool_call hook path enforces the same policy; no policy gap introduced

That distinction is required before later restart-recovery work can make conservative retry or refund decisions without guessing from promise settlement.

This is the first independently reviewable dependency extracted from #96230. The original PR remains frozen while its behavior is split into ordered, narrower changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The protocol client is the only layer that owns the synchronous `socket.send(...)` boundary, so this adds an optional `onDispatched` observer immediately after `send` returns successfully and routes it through the existing callback-isolation helper. The package client and high-level `callGateway` wrapper forward the same observer without changing request frames, protocol versions, timeout/abort cleanup, reconnect behavior, or `onAccepted` response semantics.

The observer contract is intentionally narrow: it means the request frame was handed to the local WebSocket transport. It does not mean the Gateway/server accepted or processed the request. The request option type lives in a dedicated small module and is re-exported from the existing protocol-client module, preserving import and structural type compatibility. `GatewayClient` forwards that shared option shape as a unit, then overrides only its normalized `expectFinal` and `timeoutMs` values; this keeps the oversized implementation LOC-neutral without deleting unrelated comments.

This is a root-cause boundary fix: higher layers no longer need to infer whether transport dispatch happened. The gateway-client package is private and the new field is additive and optional. A consumer/test-double sweep covered the package export, OpenClaw facade, SDK transport, accepted-response caller, both affected request stubs, and the node-host bridge. The node-host bridge only forwards `timeoutMs` across its IPC boundary, so later recovery code must use `callGateway` or introduce a separate IPC dispatch acknowledgement rather than assuming this observer is available there.

Out of scope for this PR: Plugin SDK/session-state isolation, recovery persistence, `mainRestartRecovery` admission or ownership, bounded recovery, quarantine, and Doctor repair. In particular, this PR does not write any production recovery state.

## User Impact

There is no direct end-user behavior change. Existing callers behave exactly as before; later recovery PRs can use a precise local transport-dispatch fact instead of broad failure inference.

Risk is limited to an additive observer callback. It is not invoked when WebSocket send throws, observer exceptions are isolated from request settlement, and the callback must not be interpreted as server acceptance.

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `4e1bc84e3e1`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `652266b8b6c`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.
